sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: US Judge Blocks Trump's Election Interference Tactics
cards.content: a US federal judge has issued an emergency order to halt the Trump administration's aggressive tactics to pressure election officials across the country, citing concerns that these actions may interfere with election administration and disenfranchise lawful voters. The order, which expires on November 16, bars the Justice Department and the Department of Homeland Security from demanding that election officials segregate ballots, purge voters from voter rolls, or halt ballot processing. The judge's ruling also blocks threats of criminal prosecutions against election officials and prohibits the administration from taking actions that 'threaten, intimidate or coerce' election officials. This decision comes as part of a lawsuit brought by a coalition of labor unions and civil rights groups, which claims the administration's recent conduct violates the Voting Rights Act and amounts to an unconstitutional intrusion into state control over election administration.

cards.title: Elon Musk spends $445M on US politics, backs Texas Senate race
cards.content: Elon Musk, the world's richest man, has contributed nearly half a billion dollars to federal committees, making him the single largest disclosed donor in modern American politics. He has spent over $445 million, with nearly $216 million going to his own super PAC, America PAC. Musk's money has been deployed in Texas, where he lives, and is playing a significant role in the Senate race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton. Musk's PAC has funded mailers, digital advertising, and other outreach to Texas voters, while also supporting the Senate Leadership Fund and Texas PAC, which has issued attacks against Talarico. The spending has outpaced Talarico's campaign, with Democrats being outspent by Republicans on ads by more than 2 to 1 in the final four weeks of the election.

cards.title: Russia Shuts Down Novaya Gazeta After 30 Years
cards.content: . Novaya Gazeta, Russia's most prominent independent newspaper, is being shut down after thirty years. The paper's journalists are being targeted by the Russian authorities, who accuse Novaya Gazeta of being a foreign agent. The paper has been facing increasing pressure since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with new laws aimed at punishing dissent and silencing criticism. This has led to the blocking of the paper's websites, revocation of its media license, and refusal of donations. Journalist and co-founder Dmitry Muratov, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021, believes the paper is being strangled by the authorities. This is not the first time Novaya Gazeta has faced attacks; six colleagues have been killed for their work, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was shot dead twenty years ago. The paper's closure is seen as a blow to freedom of expression and democracy in Russia.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Researchers Develop Flexible, Conductive Shielding Materials
cards.content: Researchers are developing a new generation of electromagnetic shielding materials that combine excellent conductivity with strength and flexibility. Currently, options like metals, polymers, and carbon-based materials can be heavy, inflexible, or expensive. A promising approach combines two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) with nanocellulose, a lightweight material from natural biomass. This combination offers excellent conductivity and chemical stability, but adding nanocellulose improves mechanical strength while preserving electrical properties. A research team led by Prof. Ming-Guo Ma has published a comprehensive review of MXene/nanocellulose composites, examining their structure, fabrication methods, and strengthening mechanisms. The review highlights differences between one-dimensional fibers, two-dimensional layered films, and three-dimensional networks, as well as various strengthening approaches, manufacturing techniques, and challenges. The goal is to create high-performance shielding materials that can adjust their electromagnetic behavior in response to changing conditions.

cards.title: Christie's pharmacy training inspired detective novels
cards.content: Before becoming a renowned author, Agatha Christie worked in a chemist's shop in Torquay, England, where she witnessed dark behaviors from a mysterious employer, Mr. P, who carried a deadly poison. Christie's sharp mind caught a mistake he made while infusing drugs and prevented a dangerous situation. Her experiences in the shop sparked the idea for her gripping detective novels, which were later inspired by her pharmacy training. Christie's accurate descriptions of poisons, which served as murder weapons in 41 of her 66 detective novels, continue to impress readers and experts today. Her work not only entertained but also educated readers about the science of poisons, helping to solve real-world crimes. Christie's life experiences, from working as a nurse during World War I to her extensive pharmacy training, are subtly woven into her novels, showcasing her attention to detail and expertise in the field of medicine.

cards.title: Reddit to Require Official Accounts for All Users
cards.content: Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the platform, a significant change that comes as the company faces a decline in search-referral traffic from Google. The shift is attributed to Google's increased use of AI overviews and chatting features, which has negatively impacted Reddit's referral traffic. The change aims to focus on the company's core users who come to the platform directly, with CEO Steve Huffman stating that users will likely adapt to the new requirement. The move is part of Reddit's efforts to grow its user base and increase revenue, with the company's third-quarter sales growing 53% year-over-year. Reddit will begin testing the new account requirement in the fourth quarter outside of the US, with Huffman emphasizing the company's focus on logged-in users who are more active and valuable to advertisers.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: AML treatment shows promise in mice and cancer cells
cards.content: Researchers have developed an experimental treatment for acute myeloid leukemia (AML), a type of cancer that affects blood and bone marrow. The treatment, which targets the energy demands of malignant cells, uses a molecule called AcTor to block a signaling protein involved in controlling a protein called mTOR. When combined with a drug called ixazomib, the treatment disrupts energy production in mitochondria, causing cancer cells to experience severe stress and die. The treatment has shown promising results in mice and patient-derived cancer cells, including a particularly aggressive form of the disease. The researchers hope that this approach will eventually lead to a cure for AML.

cards.title: Stenting, Surgery No Boost to Cognitive Skills, Study Finds
cards.content: A recent study led by Randolph Marshall at Columbia University found that opening severely narrowed carotid arteries, also known as stenting or surgery, does not improve cognitive skills compared to medication alone. The study, known as CREST-H, enrolled 291 patients with carotid artery narrowing and found that cognitive scores improved slightly in both groups, but patients who underwent a procedure did no better than those treated with medication alone. This challenges the idea that reopening these arteries can reverse cognitive decline in patients without associated symptoms. The study's findings have already changed practice, with more patients receiving stents, but the results suggest that patients should not expect the procedure to improve their thinking skills beyond what medication alone provides.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Australia's fossil fuel exports emit 12.4 billion tonnes of CO2e
cards.content: Australia's fossil fuel exports between 2016 and 2026 produced an estimated 12.4 billion tonnes of CO2e emissions, surpassing the combined domestic emissions of the world's 44 least developed countries. The majority, 78%, was due to coal, which contributed 9.7 billion tonnes of emissions. Australia has reduced its domestic emissions by 29% since 2005, but continues to approve coal and gas projects, raising questions about its climate commitments. The country's fossil fuel exports emitted emissions equivalent to around a third of the European Union's domestic emissions, and the total emissions could reach 19.3 billion tonnes by 2032. This is concerning as it would account for 3.4% of the remaining global carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C. The emissions refer to those released when Australian fossil fuels are burned overseas, not within Australia.

cards.title: Antarctica Turns Green and Red Due to Penguin Droppings Fueling Algae
cards.content: Antarctica, known for its vast expanses of white ice and snow-covered mountains, is unexpectedly turning green and red in some areas. This phenomenon has caught the attention of scientists who are trying to understand the connection to climate change. One factor contributing to the colorful patches is penguin droppings, which provide nutrients to microscopic algae growing on the snow. The scientists suspect that this natural process may accelerate local melting, adding to the effects of a warming climate. The impact of penguin droppings on the melting of Antarctica's snow is still being studied, and the effects are not yet fully understood.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Kettering Cinema Revival: Community Screenings Begin October 30
cards.content: A film enthusiast, Will Preston, is working to revive cinema screenings in Kettering, Northamptonshire, after the closure of the Odeon cinema in January 2025. The Odeon, which opened in 1997, was shut down due to a significant drop in attendance over the past five years. Preston, who has fond memories of visiting the cinema with his family, is organizing community screenings at various locations in Kettering. The first event is scheduled for October 30, with plans to hold monthly screenings. Preston aims to make the cinema experience accessible and affordable for the community, with tickets and snacks priced cheaply. In 2024, over 2,000 people signed a petition to save the Kettering Odeon, and now Preston is working to bring back the cinematic experience to the town.

cards.title: Traitors contestant lands lead roles and business success after reality TV appearance
cards.content: Former The Traitors contestant Kieran Tompsett, 46, from Stevenage, Hertfordshire, has transformed his life after appearing on the show in 2022. He decided to attend Ashley Walters' Kingdom Drama School, training for a year and a half and landing roles in three or four films, including Masters of the Universe. Tompsett was initially overwhelmed by the loss of privacy that came with being in the public eye, but he has since secured a lead role in a horror film and runs an AI workflow automation company. He will also appear in the dark comedy Damaged Goods. Prior to The Traitors, Tompsett worked as a solutions consultant.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: White House Tries to Bridge Economic Data Gap with Voters' Perceptions
cards.content: The White House is facing a familiar dilemma, where economic numbers aren't necessarily bad, but the public mood is. The issue is the disconnect between the solid economic data, such as low unemployment and strong growth, and the high prices that voters are paying at supermarkets and gas stations. President Donald Trump has promised to bring prices down, but the latest inflation report confirms that prices remain high. Trump's administration has tried to shift the focus from prices to economic indicators like GDP and the stock market, but voters are judging the economy by what they pay at the supermarket and whether they can keep up with bills. The challenge for Trump is to bridge the gap between the economic data and the public's perception of the economy. His predecessor, Joe Biden, faced a similar challenge during the 2024 election campaign, but ultimately failed to convince voters that the economy was working for them.

cards.title: Naomi Nomi Revolutionizes Fashion with Quality, Long-Lasting Clothing
cards.content: Naomi Mishkin, the founder of Naomi Nomi, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by producing high-quality, long-lasting clothing at a higher price point. The average customer starts with one shirt and returns for three more within six months, as they realize the value of her products. Mishkin's approach is a departure from the fast fashion industry, which has mastered the art of cutting production costs to the bone. She uses cotton and wool, making her shirts pricier than fast fashion, but lasting longer. Naomi Nomi's success is attributed to the growing backlash against companies that prioritize profit over quality and the environment. The fashion industry has undergone significant changes over the past few decades, with a shift towards planned obsolescence and the use of cheaper materials. However, some consumers are now looking for brands that offer quality, durability, and sustainability, and Naomi Nomi is capitalizing on this trend.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
